column1: # ⛔ THIS FILE IS HAND-MAINTAINED AND MUST NEVER BE GENERATED.
# It exists because the generated index cannot constrain its own shrinkage:
#     delete a test                  -> test-authority.py check FAILS
#     delete a test + regenerate     -> the index tracks the smaller reality, silently
# Regeneration is routine, so the index describes what IS. This floor constrains
# whether what IS may shrink without a human saying so.
# ⛔ THE FLOOR MUST NOT DERIVE FROM THE INDEX IT CONSTRAINS. If test-authority.py
# ever writes this file, the control becomes tautological:
#     delete -> regenerate index -> regenerate floor -> green.
# LOWERING the floor is a deliberate act: edit the value, state why, and let it show
# in review. RAISING it is routine and may accompany any PR that adds tests.

column2: RAISED 308 -> 313 in v1.229.7 PR-4. This single raise covers FIVE guards the v1.229.7 mode-authority lane added, and only one of them belongs to this PR: daemon_callable_neutrality (PR-2), module_orchestrator_unbound_var (PR-2a), mode_plan_exclusivity (PR-3A), plan_projection (PR-3B) and read_path_mode_contract (PR-4). The four earlier ones merged WITHOUT raising the floor. Each of those PRs passed the floor check legitimately -- 313 >= 308 -- because slack absorbed them, so the control silently stopped covering the work the lane was adding: all five could have been deleted and the check would still have gone green. SLACK IS NOT COVERAGE. Raising to 313 restores the floor's actual purpose, which is to make shrinkage of the CURRENT estate a deliberate act.
